html:
A small Portuguese settlement on the south China coast, on a peninsula at the mouth of the Pearl River, held from 1557 until it was handed back to China in 1999. It was the first European foothold in China and the last to go.

Portuguese traders, after their capture of Malacca, reached China in the 1510s. Around 1557 the Ming let them settle at Macau, for a rent, in exchange for help against pirates. Macau then boomed as the link in a triangle trade: Chinese silk went to Japan for silver, and the silver bought more Chinese goods. It was also the base for Jesuits such as Matteo Ricci.

For three centuries China still claimed the land. Portugal only declared full control in 1849 and won a treaty recognising it in 1887. Macau was overshadowed by British Hong Kong after 1842 and lived from gambling and smuggling. Under a 1987 agreement it returned to the People's Republic as a special region, now known for its casinos.
